migration.name: 20260815190000_cross_domain_ruling_material_tags
migration.backfill: Value-only backfill of an existing String[] column; no column added, altered, or dropped, and no row created or deleted. Appends the 'all-business-domains' topic tag to PerspectiveMaterial rows that are already ruled-tier owner rulings (sourceType='stance' AND evidenceGrade='A' AND confidenceWeight>=1.0 AND promotionState='promoted' AND reviewStatus='approved'). Idempotent: rows already carrying the tag are skipped via NOT ('all-business-domains' = ANY(domains)), so a re-run is a no-op. Deliberately narrow — archetype defaults (unconfirmed, 0.6) and owner settings confirmations (confirmed, 0.9) are untouched, so only an explicit human ruling gains cross-domain reach. Reversible by removing the tag from the same predicate; no information is lost because the original domainClass column is unmodified.

changes.lifecycleDisposition: No row is created, deleted, or re-tiered. Existing ruled-tier rows gain one additional topic tag on an existing array column; domainClass, confidenceWeight, evidenceGrade, reviewStatus, and promotionState are all left exactly as they were. The material ladder is unchanged — this widens where a ruling can be RETRIEVED, never what authority it carries.

fields.reason: domains[] is a dormant topic-tag array that already exists on the model and until now only ever mirrored domainClass. It becomes load-bearing because isMaterialApplicable now matches additively over it. The backfill carries no data about a person: the tag is a static string constant, and the rows it lands on are the organization's own published doctrine. It exists to repair a retrieval defect — an owner ruling filed under one caller-supplied domainClass was invisible to the same question bucketed under another, so answering a decision taught the corpus something it could never retrieve (live evidence: DI-3A99C3561FA0 excluded stances/ruling-di-5bc09b3e5683).
